335271.title: The odd-order edge lower-bound conjecture for k-in-out graphs
335271.statement:
A **$k$-in-out graph** is a directed graph satisfying the single visit and paired vertices conditions, with parameter $k$. For odd $k$, consider such graphs of order $2k+1$.

**Odd-order edge lower-bound conjecture.** Any $k$-in-out graph of order $2k+1$ for odd $k$ has at least $4k-3$ edges.

The construction discussed in the source has $4k-3$ edges for odd $k$, while the general lower bound known there is only $4k-4$. No examples with $4k-4$ edges were known for odd $k$, motivating this conjecture.

other_fields.title: The odd-order edge lower-bound conjecture for k-in-out graphs
other_fields.source_name: David Glynn, Michael Haythorpe and Asghar Moeini, “A construction for directed in-out subgraphs of optimal size”, arXiv:1702.03075 (2018).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.03075

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

335352.title: Permutation conjecture for a rational function on roots of unity
335352.statement:
Let $k$ be an even integer and set $q=5^k$. Let

$$
\mu_{q+1}=\{x\in {\mathbb F}_{q^2}:x^{q+1}=1\}
$$

be the group of $(q+1)$-st roots of unity in ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$. **Permutation conjecture.** The rational function

$$
-x\left(\frac{x^2-2}{x^2+2}\right)^2
$$

permutes $\mu_{q+1}$.
If true, this would yield a class of permutation trinomials over finite fields through the relation between permutation polynomials over ${\mathbb F}_{q^2}$ and rational functions on $\mu_{q+1}$ described in the surrounding argument.

other_fields.title: Permutation conjecture for a rational function on roots of unity
other_fields.source_name: Gaofei Wu and Nian Li, “Several Classes of Permutation Trinomials over F_5^n From Niho Exponents”, arXiv:1702.06446 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.06446

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2017).

335382.title: Existence of angle labelings for essentially 3-connected maps
335382.statement:
Let $G$ be a map on a genus $g\geq 1$ orientable surface. An **edge, positive-vertex, positive-face angle labeling** means a labeling with the edge condition and positive vertex and face conditions indicated by those parameters. A map is **essentially 3-connected** when its universal-cover graph is 3-connected in the relevant essential sense. **The angle-labeling conjecture.** $G$ admits an edge, $\mathbb{N}^*$-vertex, $\mathbb{N}^*$-face angle labeling if and only if it is essentially 3-connected.

The “only if” direction is supported by the cited proposition and lemma; the converse is proposed as the general-map analogue of the preceding triangulation conjecture.

other_fields.title: Existence of angle labelings for essentially 3-connected maps
other_fields.source_name: Benjamin Lévêque, “Generalization of Schnyder woods to orientable surfaces and applications”, arXiv:1702.07589 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.07589

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2017); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

335553.title: The regularity conjecture for the $k$-abelian complexity of automatic sequences
335553.statement:
Let $k\geq 1$ and let $\omega$ be an $\ell$-automatic sequence, meaning that its $\ell$-kernel is finite. The $k$-abelian complexity of $\omega$ is the sequence counting the $k$-abelian equivalence classes of factors of each length.

**Automatic-sequence regularity conjecture.** The $k$-abelian complexity of any $\ell$-automatic sequence is an $\ell$-regular sequence.

The conjecture generalizes the previously conjectured—and independently proved—case of the $2$-abelian complexity of the Thue–Morse sequence. The paper presents the $3$-regularity of the $k$-abelian complexity of the Cantor sequence as supporting evidence; the general assertion remains open in the supplied source.

other_fields.title: The regularity conjecture for the $k$-abelian complexity of automatic sequences
other_fields.source_name: Jin Chen, Xiaotao Lü and Wen Wu, “On the k-abelian complexity of the Cantor sequence”, arXiv:1703.04063 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.04063

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2017). “This is proved in and independently.”

335668.title: Adjacency-spectral determination conjecture for complements of multicone cycle graphs
335668.statement: Let $K_w$ be the complete graph on $w$ vertices, let $C_n$ be the cycle graph on $n$ vertices, and let $mC_n$ denote the disjoint union of $m$ copies of $C_n$. Write $G\bigtriangledown H$ for the join of graphs $G$ and $H$, and let $\overline{G}$ denote the complement of $G$. A graph is **DS with respect to its adjacency spectrum** if every graph with the same adjacency spectrum is isomorphic to it. **Complementary multicone conjecture.** The graphs $\overline{K_w\bigtriangledown mC_n}$ are DS with respect to their adjacency spectra. The source establishes this for some cases, including $\overline{K_w\bigtriangledown mC_3}$ and $\overline{K_w\bigtriangledown C_4}$, while the general claim remains unresolved in the source.

other_fields.title: Adjacency-spectral determination conjecture for complements of multicone cycle graphs
other_fields.source_name: Ali Zeydi Abdian, “The spectral determinations of the multicone graphs Kw+mCn”, arXiv:1703.08728 (2018).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.08728

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

335721.title: Deletion conjecture for unavoidable formulas with reversal
335721.statement:
Let $phi$ be a formula with reversal, and let $X$ be its set of two-way variables. Write $delta_{X\cup X^R}(phi)$ for the formula obtained by deleting all occurrences of the two-way variables in $X$ and their reversals $X^R$.

**Deletion conjecture.** If $phi$ is unavoidable, then $delta_{X\cup X^R}(phi)$ is unavoidable.

This conjecture is proposed as a possible route toward the generalized Zimin divisibility conjecture. The paper notes that the analogous factor property for one-way variables does not generalize directly when there are at least three one-way variables, while the preservation of unavoidability after deleting two-way variables remains plausible and open.

other_fields.title: Deletion conjecture for unavoidable formulas with reversal
other_fields.source_name: James Daniel Currie, Lucas Mol and Narad Rampersad, “On avoidability of formulas with reversal”, arXiv:1703.10522 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1703.10522

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2017).

335976.title: Fraenkel's conjecture on complementary Beatty sequences
335976.statement:
Let $d\geq 3$, let $\alpha_1<\alpha_2<\ldots<\alpha_d$, and let $\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_d$ be real numbers. Suppose that the vectors

$$
(\lfloor n\alpha_i+\gamma_i\rfloor)_{i=1}^d,
$$

for $n\in\mathbb{N}$, split the positive integers. **Fraenkel's conjecture.** Then

$$
\alpha_i=\frac{2^d-1}{2^{d-i}},\qquad i=1,\ldots,d.
$$

This is the nonhomogeneous rational-modulus form of Fraenkel's conjecture on partitions of the positive integers by Beatty-type sequences. The statement concerns the uniqueness of the moduli, while the shifts $\gamma_i$ are unrestricted; the source presents it as a conjecture and gives historical references to work on special cases.

other_fields.title: Fraenkel's conjecture on complementary Beatty sequences
other_fields.source_name: Aviezri S. Fraenkel and Urban Larsson, “Playability and arbitrarily large rat games”, arXiv:1705.03061 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.03061

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

336029.title: The Grid-associahedron as a facet reduction of a polytope
336029.statement:
Let $\lambda$ be a shape, let $\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}=\{H_s:s\in\operatorname{Seg}(\lambda)\}$ be the arrangement associated with its segments, and let $\mathcal{F}_{\lambda}$ be the Grid-associahedron fan. **Facet-reduction conjecture.** There exists a polytope $P$ whose normal fan is $\mathcal{A}_{\lambda}$ such that the Grid-associahedron, whose normal fan is $\mathcal{F}_{\lambda}$, may be constructed by removing some facets from $P$.

This conjecture seeks a direct polyhedral construction parallel to the construction of associahedra from permutahedra by removing facets. The fan poset is a quotient lattice of the lattice of biclosed subsets, but the required polytope and facet-removal construction remain open.

other_fields.title: The Grid-associahedron as a facet reduction of a polytope
other_fields.source_name: Alexander Garver and Thomas McConville, “Enumerative properties of Grid-Associahedra”, arXiv:1705.04901 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.04901

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2017). “As an application, we obtain a bijection between the facets of the nonkissing complex and of the noncrossing complex, which provides a partial solution to an open problem of Santos, Stump, and Welker.”

336226.title: Zvonkine's topological-recursion conjecture for orbifold $r$-spin Hurwitz numbers
336226.statement:
Let $g\geq 0$ and $n\geq 1$. For positive integers $\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n$, let $h_{g;\mu}^{\circ,q,r}$ be the connected $q$-orbifold $r$-spin Hurwitz number, and define the formal symmetric $n$-differential

$$
W_{g,n}(x_1,\ldots,x_n)=d_1\otimes\cdots\otimes d_n\sum_{\mu_1,\ldots,\mu_n=1}^{\infty}h_{g;\mu}^{\circ,q,r}\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{\mu_i}.
$$

Let $\omega_{g,n}(z_1,\ldots,z_n)$ be symmetric $n$-differentials on the spectral curve with parametrization $x(z)=ze^{-z^{qr}}$ and $y(z)=z^q$. **Zvonkine's topological-recursion conjecture.** The formal differentials $W_{g,n}$ are expansions in $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ of the differentials $\omega_{g,n}$, and the latter satisfy topological recursion on this spectral curve.

other_fields.title: Zvonkine's topological-recursion conjecture for orbifold $r$-spin Hurwitz numbers
other_fields.source_name: Gaëtan Borot, Reinier Kramer, Danilo Lewanski, Alexandr Popolitov and Sergey Shadrin, “Special cases of the orbifold version of Zvonkine's r-ELSV formula”, arXiv:1705.10811 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1705.10811

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2017).

336252.title: Shuffle-compatibility of the up-down run and peak statistics
336252.statement:
Let a **permutation statistic** assign an invariant to each permutation, and call it **shuffle-compatible** if, for any two disjoint permutations, the multiset of its values on their shuffles depends only on the two input statistics. Let $\operatorname{udr}$ denote the up-down run statistic, $\operatorname{pk}$ the peak statistic, and $\operatorname{des}$ the descent statistic. **The up-down run–peak shuffle-compatibility conjecture.** The tuples

$$
(\operatorname{udr},\operatorname{pk})
$$

and

$$
(\operatorname{udr},\operatorname{pk},\operatorname{des})
$$

are shuffle-compatible. This is one of the paper's empirically supported conjectures about joint permutation statistics; its resolution is not given in the source.

other_fields.title: Shuffle-compatibility of the up-down run and peak statistics
other_fields.source_name: Ira M. Gessel and Yan Zhuang, “Shuffle-compatible permutation statistics”, arXiv:1706.00750 (2018).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.00750

Status: **open** according to the source (as of June 2017). “To conclude this paper, we state a couple permutation statistics that we conjecture to be shuffle-compatible based on empirical evidence, and a few more general open problems and conjectures on the topic of shuffle-compatibility.”

336454.title: The Colin de Verdière graph complement conjecture
336454.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite simple graph and let $\overline{G}$ denote its complement. Let $\mu(G)$ denote the Colin de Verdière parameter. **Colin de Verdière's graph complement conjecture.** Every graph $G$ satisfies

$$
\mu(G)+\mu(\overline{G})\geq |V(G)|-2.
$$

This is the complement analogue of Nordhaus–Gaddum-type inequalities for graph parameters and is related in the paper to the extremal edge conjecture for the Colin de Verdière parameter. The source presents it as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied there.

other_fields.title: The Colin de Verdière graph complement conjecture
other_fields.source_name: Rose McCarty, “The Extremal Function and Colin de Verdière Graph Parameter”, arXiv:1706.07451 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.07451

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2017).

336558.title: Little-o upper-bound conjecture for equal-weight separating hash families
336558.statement:
Let $C(N,q,\{w_1,\ldots,w_t\})$ be the maximal size of an $SHF(N;n,q,\{w_1,\ldots,w_t\})$. Let $t\ge 3$ be a positive integer, set $w_1=\cdots=w_t=1$, and assume $(t-1)\nmid N$.

**Little-o upper-bound conjecture.**

$$
C(N,q,\{1,\ldots,1\})=o\left(q^{\left\lceil\frac{N}{t-1}\right\rceil}\right).
$$

The conjecture concerns the nondivisible-length case, where the known general upper bound may or may not be of the correct order. The source notes that the claim is known when $N=t\ge 3$, while the general case remains open; attempted use of the hypergraph removal lemma did not resolve it.

other_fields.title: Little-o upper-bound conjecture for equal-weight separating hash families
other_fields.source_name: Gennian Ge, Chong Shangguan and Xin Wang, “Some intriguing upper bounds for separating hash families”, arXiv:1707.01758 (2018).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.01758

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of July 2017). “Indeed, recently the correctness of this conjecture was confirmed by the first two authors of this paper in .”

336567.title: The even-dimensional weight-distribution conjecture for the design codes
336567.statement:
Let $m\geq 4$ be even. Let $\mathbb{D}=({\mathcal{P}},{\mathcal{B}}_2)$ be the $2$-design in Theorem 5, or let $\mathbb{D}=({\mathcal{P}},{\mathcal{B}})$ be the $2$-design in Theorem 4, and let ${\mathcal{C}}_2(\mathbb{D})$ denote its binary code. **The even-dimensional design-code conjecture.** The code ${\mathcal{C}}_2(\mathbb{D})$ has parameters

$$
[2^m,\,2m+1,\,2^{m-1}-2^{m/2}],
$$

and has the weight distribution displayed in the paper's table. In addition, the dual code ${\mathcal{C}}_2(\mathbb{D})^\perp$ has parameters $[2^m,2^m-1-2m,6]$.

This is presented as a conjectured extension for the even-dimensional cases of the two design families. The source provides the claimed parameters and refers to a table for the full distribution; no resolution is given.

other_fields.title: The even-dimensional weight-distribution conjecture for the design codes
other_fields.source_name: Hao Liu and Cunsheng Ding, “Infinite families of 2-designs from GA_1(q) actions”, arXiv:1707.02003 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.02003

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

336620.title: Mubayi–Stein threshold conjecture for tight-path Ramsey parameters
336620.statement:
For integers $3\leq t\leq k$, let $\overline r_k(k+1,t;P_n)$ be the least $N$ such that every red/blue coloring of the $k$-sets of an $N$-vertex set contains a blue tight path $P_n$ or has a $(k+1)$-vertex set inducing at least $t$ red edges. Define $\operatorname{twr}_1(x)=x$ and $\operatorname{twr}_{i+1}(x)=2^{\operatorname{twr}_i(x)}$. **Mubayi–Stein conjecture.** There are positive constants $c=c(k,t)$ and $c'=c'(k,t)$ such that

$$
\operatorname{twr}_{t-2}(n^c)<\overline r_k(k+1,t;P_n)<\operatorname{twr}_{t-2}(n^{c'}).
$$

This is the tight-path analogue of the Erdős–Hajnal tower-growth conjecture for cliques. The source presents it as open.

other_fields.title: Mubayi–Stein threshold conjecture for tight-path Ramsey parameters
other_fields.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Andrew Suk, “A survey of hypergraph Ramsey problems”, arXiv:1707.04229 (2018).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.04229

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

336651.title: Colorability conjecture for cyclic pseudo-Loupekine graphs with parity conditions
336651.statement: Let $S$ be a Loupekine 5-pole, let $x\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, and let $S_x(m;a,a,c)$ denote the associated cyclic pseudo-Loupekine graph. Assume that $m/\gcd(m,a)$ is even and $m/\gcd(m,c)$ is odd. **Cyclic pseudo-Loupekine colorability conjecture.** All such graphs $S_x(m;a,a,c)$ are 3-edge-colorable. This conjecture concerns a broad generalization of Loupekine's construction; the supplied text gives no resolution or partial proof.

other_fields.title: Colorability conjecture for cyclic pseudo-Loupekine graphs with parity conditions
other_fields.source_name: Leah Wrenn Berman, Déborah Oliveros and Gordon I. Williams, “Cyclic pseudo-Loupekine snarks”, arXiv:1707.05294 (2019).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.05294

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

336652.title: Cyclic 5-connectivity conjecture for the T families
336652.statement: Let $T^1_\alpha(m;a,a,c)$, $T^1_\beta(m;a,a,c)$, and $T^2_\alpha(m;a,a,c)$ be the snark families defined from the two triangle-destroying deletions of the Petersen-derived 5-pole. **Cyclic 5-connectivity conjecture.** If $m/\gcd(m,c)>4$, then the infinite families of snarks $T^1_\alpha(m;a,a,c)$ and $T^1_\beta(m;a,a,c)$ are cyclically 5-connected. The text reports computational checks for several small cases, but no general proof is given.

other_fields.title: Cyclic 5-connectivity conjecture for the T families
other_fields.source_name: Leah Wrenn Berman, Déborah Oliveros and Gordon I. Williams, “Cyclic pseudo-Loupekine snarks”, arXiv:1707.05294 (2019).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.05294

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

336718.title: Positivity conjecture for matrix counts of a complementary diagonal permutation
336718.statement: For a positive integer $n$, let $v=(2n-1)(2n)(2n-3)(2n-2)\cdots3412$ be the indicated permutation, and let $I_v$ be its diagram. Write $M_{2n}(\overline{I_v},q)$ for the matrix count of rank-$2n$ matrices over $\mathbf{F}_q$ supported in the complement of $I_v$. **Positivity conjecture.** For $v=(2n-1)(2n)(2n-3)(2n-2)\cdots3412$, $M_{2n}(\overline{I_v},q)$ belongs to $\mathbb{N}[q]$. Computations in the source verify this for $n\leq40$, but the general assertion is left as a conjecture.

other_fields.title: Positivity conjecture for matrix counts of a complementary diagonal permutation
other_fields.source_name: Joel Brewster Lewis and Alejandro H. Morales, “Rook theory of the finite general linear group”, arXiv:1707.08192 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.08192

Status: **open** according to the source (as of July 2017). “We also offer a weak conjecture that is certainly a precondition for an affirmative answer to Question .”

336736.title: The feasibility interval for the undirected optical-index ratio
336736.statement:
Let $\delta\geq 1$ be a rational number. Call $\delta$ **feasible** if there exists a simple graph $G$ such that

$$
\frac{w(G)}{\pi(G)}=\delta.
$$

**The feasibility-interval conjecture.** Any rational number $\delta$ satisfying

$$
1\leq\delta\leq\frac{3}{2}
$$

is feasible.
The paper establishes feasibility for several infinite families of values, including values arising from complete $m$-ary trees. Whether every rational number in the interval is feasible remains open.

other_fields.title: The feasibility interval for the undirected optical-index ratio
other_fields.source_name: Yuan-Hsun Lo, Hung-Lin Fu, Yijin Zhang and Wing Shing Wong, “The Undirected Optical Indices of Complete m-ary Trees”, arXiv:1707.09745 (2018).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.09745

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).

336742.title: The four-list conjecture for facial unique-maximum edge-coloring
336742.statement:
Let $G$ be a plane graph. A **FUM-edge-coloring** is a facial edge-coloring in which every face is incident with a unique edge colored with the maximal color appearing on that face. Suppose each edge $e$ is assigned a list $L(e)$ of four integers.

**Four-list conjecture.** If each edge of a plane graph is assigned a list of $4$ integers, then there exists a FUM-edge-coloring assigning each edge a color from its list.

This is the list-coloring analogue of the proposed four-color bound for FUM-edge-coloring. The source presents it as an expectation and gives no resolution, so it remains open.

other_fields.title: The four-list conjecture for facial unique-maximum edge-coloring
other_fields.source_name: Vesna Andova, Bernard Lidický, Borut Lužar and Riste Škrekovski, “On facial unique-maximum (edge-)coloring”, arXiv:1708.00094 (2017).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.00094

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).

336747.title: Polynomial domination conjecture for directed-triangle-free digraphs
336747.statement:
Let $G$ be a digraph. A digraph is **directed-triangle-free** if it contains no directed cycle of length three, $\alpha(G)$ denotes its independence number, and $\gamma(G)$ denotes its domination number.

**Polynomial domination conjecture.** There is an integer $\ell$ such that if $G$ is a directed-triangle-free digraph with $\alpha(D)=\alpha$, then

$$
\gamma(G)\leq\alpha^{\ell}.
$$

This is the domination-number consequence of the conjecture that the dichromatic number of a directed-triangle-free digraph is bounded by a polynomial in its independence number. The source presents it as a conjecture; no resolution is supplied here.

other_fields.title: Polynomial domination conjecture for directed-triangle-free digraphs
other_fields.source_name: Ararat Harutyunyan, Tien-Nam Le, Alantha Newman and Stéphan Thomassé, “Domination and fractional domination in digraphs”, arXiv:1708.00423 (2018).
other_fields.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.00423

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2017).
